basics.name: Thinh Nguyen Nhu
basics.label: Mechatronics Engineer & AI Researcher
basics.summary: As a science-oriented person, my long-term vision is to develop intelligent systems and structures that learn from the fundamental principles of physics, biology, and engineering. My research interests focus on applied machine learning, particularly Physics-Informed Machine Learning (PIML) and Generative AI for scientific discovery and inverse problems. My ultimate goal is to build physics-grounded AI models that enable the understanding, design, and control of next-generation smart systems.

location.address: Hanoi University of Science and Technology

work.name: AiRA Lab, HUST
work.summary: Investigate Physics-Informed Machine Learning (PIML), DNA Origami simulations, and AI4SE teaching assistance.
highlights: Investigate Physics-Informed Machine Learning (PIML) methods for scientific and engineering applications.
Develop PINN architectures for multi-solution inverse design of Kresling Origami structures.
Conduct molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and structural design of DNA Origami; explore AI-driven approaches for DNA Origami property prediction and design.
Serve as Teaching Assistant for the course AI for Science and Engineering (AI4SE) (https://github.com/AiRA-Laboratory/AI4SE).

work.name: ICMAM Lab Collaborative, HCMUT
work.summary: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for structural analysis and optimization of composite laminates.
highlights: Apply Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINN) for structural analysis and design optimization of composite laminates based on First-order Shear Deformation Theory (FSDT).

work.name: Origami Technology Lab, HUST
work.summary: Modeled nonlinear dynamic behaviors of Kresling origami, developed PINN algorithms, and numerical dynamic simulation of magnetically actuated origami.
highlights: Modeled nonlinear dynamic behaviors of Kresling origami and constructed bifurcation diagrams under harmonic excitation.
Formulated Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) algorithms for the inverse design of Kresling structures as part of undergraduate thesis research.
Perform numerical dynamic modeling of Magnetically Actuated Kresling Origami combining magnetic actuation with a bar-and-hinge framework and the open-source Newton-Physics environment.

work.name: Project XYaZ Lab, HUST
work.summary: Dynamics modeling and trajectory-tracking of parallel mechanisms.
highlights: Modeled and simulated the dynamics of a 3-RRR planar parallel robot using MATLAB/Simulink.
Evaluated trajectory-tracking algorithms for parallel mechanisms.
